We spent $2M telling the world to stop hiring humans.\
\
Today we’re taking it back.\
\
And in even more shocking news: Artisan is hiring a human BDR.\
\
The billboards were never a lie. Ava the AI BDR does outreach better than most humans. But she can’t legally cold call. She can’t shake a hand at a conference. She can’t be human.\
\
So we built the tools for the humans. A dialer and a full rep toolkit, inside Artisan. Your reps do the human work. Ava does EVERYTHING else. Leads, signals, personalization, objections, meetings booked, all autonomous.\
\
That’s already how the biggest teams on Artisan run. One of them has Ava working alongside 1,000+ human reps.\
\
Now we’re proving the super-BDR thesis on ourselves. The one BDR we hire will outperform most companies’ entire team. \
\
Stop hiring humans led to billions of impressions and millions in ARR. But it’s time for the next era.\
\
Next Monday: our manifesto and new slogan. The future is humans AND AI, not humans or AI.

That’s @getartisan — the SF startup building human-like AI employees to replace your bloated GTM stack… and maybe kick off the next Industrial Revolution.\
\
In this episode of TALKS WITH DASHA, I sat down with @jasparcj to talk about what it takes to build a successful company.

Artisan, the AI sales agent startup founded by Jaspar Carmichael-Jack, recently raised $25 million in Series A funding, led by Glade Brook Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, Day One Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, and others. Founded in 2024, Artisan initially garnered attention with its bold “Stop Hiring Humans” campaign, positioning itself in the rapidly growing AI sales development representative (SDR) market. Despite early-stage challenges, including customer churn and issues with AI performance, the company has made significant strides, refining its AI agent, Ava, and achieving $5 million in annual recurring revenue with 250 customers. Artisan is also working on new AI products, such as Aaron for inbound messaging and Aria, a meeting manager assistant, both set to launch by the end of 2025. Carmichael-Jack, who co-founded the company with Sam Stallings, continues to steer Artisan as CEO, emphasizing the importance of human labor in AI-driven environments.\

A small course correction now can make a much bigger difference by Black Friday.\
\
If your e-commerce brand is drifting away from plan, look upstream. Where did the gap start, and what can you change before it gets bigger?\
\
The earlier you spot the problem, the more time you have to adjust. Waiting until the results are in leaves you with fewer options.\
\
Take a look at where you are today, compare it with where you need to be, and make the correction while there’s still time.

If your team can’t move without you, the answer isn’t to make every decision yourself. Set clear goals, give people numbers they own, and build a weekly rhythm that keeps everyone aligned—even when you’re away.

I took how much money I wanted to make ($500,000) and divided it by the number of hours I wanted to work that year (1,600).\

Roughly $300 an hour.\

If you're reading this, you've probably already realized that I made a huge mistake.\

I didn't build in any time to work on the actual business. Whoops.\

\
From $300 an hour to $600 an hour.\
\
That created an entirely new problem that I hadn't considered. \
\
I could now work half as much and make the same, or I could work exactly the same amount and make double.\
\
Obviously, the first choice is the more strategic one, but the second choice is so tempting!\

One I see SO many business owners get sucked in by.\

I used that extra time to build my first courses and products, and eventually scale to more than $4M per year in profit without selling any more of my time.\

There's a really big lesson in here:\
\
You can give yourself a raise in free time, but you have to let yourself keep it.\

That time can be invested back into you and your business.\

To sell.\
To write.\
To market.\

Everything bagels made with Tesco high protein cottage cheese 💥 Recipe below ⬇️ \
\
300g cottage cheese\
300g self raising flour\
1 egg, beaten\
\
For the everything bagel seasoning\
1 tsp sesame seeds\
1 tsp poppy seeds\
½ tsp garlic granules\
½ tsp onion granules\
½ tsp flakey sea salt\
\
1. Preheat the oven to gas 6, 200°C, fan 180°C. Put the cottage cheese in a blender or food processor and blitz until smooth, then tip into a large bowl. Add the flour and season with a pinch of salt. Use your hand to mix until it forms a ball, then tip onto a lightly floured surface.\
2. Knead for 3-4 minutes until the dough is smooth. Return the dough to the bowl, cover with a tea towel and leave to rest for 15 minutes.\
3. Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces, then roll each piece into a sausage shape. Bring the two ends together and pinch to seal, creating your bagel shape. 4. Carefully stretch the dough of each bagel until the central hole is around 6cm. Then sit, spaced out, on a lined baking tray.\
5. If using, combine the bagel seasoning ingredients in a small bowl. Brush the bagels with the beaten egg then sprinkle generously with the seasoning.\
6. Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown, risen and cooked through. Allow to cool for at least 5 minutes before slicing. Enjoy as they are with butter or load them up with your favourite fillings.

Can you upgrade chilli con carne? YES! Make it brothy! 🌶️🍲 Recipe below ⬇️ \
\
For the chilli mince:\
2 tbsp olive oil\
500g 5% fat beef mince\
 1 x 400g tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed\
 1 tsp ground cumin\
 1 tsp smoked paprika\
 2 tsp garlic powder\
 2 tsp ground coriander\
 1 tsp dried oregano\
 1 tsp hot chilli powder\
\
For the broth:\
6 garlic cloves, finely minced\
 1 tbsp tomato purée\
 2 tbsp Tesco Finest Chipotle Marinade Paste\
 2 tsp ground cumin\
 2 tsp smoked paprika\
 1 tsp cinnamon\
 ½ beef stock cube, made up to 850ml\
 Juice of 1 lime\
 15g fresh coriander, finely chopped\
200g easy cook long grain & wild rice\
Fresh coriander, red pickled onions and sliced avocado, to serve (optional)\
\
1. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the beef mince, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Fry for 5-10 minutes until brown and starting to caramelise. \
2. Add the kidney beans, spices and a splash of water. Stir well and cook for another 5 minutes, or until the water has evaporated. Transfer to a bowl and keep warm.\
3. For the broth, in the same pan, combine the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the garlic, tomato purée, chipotle paste and broth spices. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.\
4. Pour in the stock and stir well. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the pack instructions. \
5. Stir the lime juice and chopped coriander into the broth. Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chilli mince. Pour over the broth and finish with fresh coriander, red pickled onions and sliced avocado, if you wish.

\

Neediness makes you cheaper.\
\
The moment a client feels how badly you need the job, the power shifts.\
\
You start discounting.\
Explaining.\
Chasing.\
Trying to make the deal happen.\
\
And ironically, that makes them want you less.\
\
The energy is simple:\
I’m good with you.\
I’m good without you.\
\
That doesn’t mean arrogance.\
\
It means believing your value doesn’t disappear because someone says no.\
\
The less desperately you need the deal, the stronger your position becomes.\

PSA: if you haven’t already, PLEASE hook up your creative folders to AI.\
\
The real ones know how much time it actually takes to track down the right assets BEFORE any editing takes place.\
\
Because of this, my team and I were able to produce AND launch 55 ads in JUST ONE DAY.\
\
Here’s the whole process we went through:\
\
1. Started with a pile of raw assets: hundreds of iPhone photos of sample product plus a few e-comm shots, all dumped into a shared @dropbox folder. No plan yet.\
\
2. Used ChatGPT for competitor research: specifically which competitor ads were pulling the highest impressions, plus mining their negative customer reviews so my product could fill that gap.\
\
3. Had ChatGPT reference the photos in the Dropbox folder and recommend which images best suited the ad angles we were about to make.\
\
4. Turned those angles into a creative matrix across the five formats and personas we wanted to target.\
\
5. Built a quick shot list from that matrix so I could film fast.\
\
6. Reviewed the recommendations, made a few edits, and saved the plan back to Dropbox  so the team could access it alongside the source images.\
\
7. Divided the work across the team and started producing the statics. Ads out within a few hours.\
\
Ngl, it’s really one of those “thank god for ai” use cases for me :)\

ROASTED CHICKEN\
Ingredients:\
\
One Whole Chicken\
Olive Oil\
Butter\
smoked paprika\
garlic\
oregano,thyme or your fave herbs (if you only have dry all good)\
kosher salt & ground black pepper\
\
Citrus, sweet onions- chopped for under the bird\
\
Method:\
Roast at 425 degrees breast side down even if. you don't spatchcock the bird for about 30 minutes or until the skin has some browning. Remove from the oven, season again and add oil, butter, citrus and herbs or whatever you like on the breast side and turn the oven down to 350 or 375 degrees and roast for another 30-45 minutes based on the size of the bird. Let it rest and cut, slice or tear apart and enjoy. \

ROASTED CHICKEN NOODLE SOUP\
Ingredients:\
1 cup sweet onion, diced\
1 shallot, diced (if you have it)\
1 cup carrots, diced\
1 cup celery, diced\
splash of sherry or marsala to deglaze the pan\
4-6 cups chicken or veggie stock, prepared\
splash of hot sauce\
2 -3 cups egg noodles, dry\
\
2 TBSP garlic, roasted or chopped\
fresh or dry herbs\
kosher salt & ground black pepper\
\
2 cups of pulled roasted chicken\
\
Method:\
I like to caramelize the veggies and the deglaze with sherry. Then drop in my hot sauce and prepared stock.  Heat all of this together for 10-15 minutes and then drop in the dry noodles and they will soak up the stock and be cooked.
